<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916904_theRebbe_178" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916904_theRebbe_178__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that just as the aspect of "face" (Panim) in souls illuminates the "back" (Achor), so too in Torah the "face" of Torah illuminates its "back," and it elaborates on the four levels of Torah—inheritance, gift, self-preparation, and bride—and their connection to the refinement of the sparks of Tohu and the distinction between the revealed and inner dimensions of Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, from this that in the souls there is drawn from the aspect of Panim also into the aspect of Achor</t>
    <t s="2">(as explained above at length)</t>
    <t s="3">it is understood that also in the Torah</t>
    <t s="4">[for He looked into the Torah and created the world104]</t>
    <t s="5">the aspect of Panim of Torah illuminates within its aspect of Achor.</t>
    <t s="6">And this will be understood based on what is explained by the Rebbe Maharash in the continuation "Vechacha" 5637</t>
    <t s="7">[for this year is the centennial year of its utterance]105</t>
    <t s="8">that in the Torah there are four aspects.</t>
    <t s="9">For it is written11</t>
    <t s="10">"Torah tzivah lanu Moshe morashah..." that the Torah was given to us as an inheritance,</t>
    <t s="11">for the word "morashah" is also a term of inheritance106,</t>
    <t s="12">and seemingly, did not our Sages say107</t>
    <t s="13">"Prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you,"</t>
    <t s="14">and this is the opposite of the exposition of "morashah" as a term of inheritance,</t>
    <t s="15">and sometimes we find in the words of our Sages108</t>
    <t s="16">that the Torah was given to us as a gift, and sometimes we find that the Torah is called a bride, according to the exposition of our Sages109</t>
    <t s="17">[on the verse "Torah tzivah lanu..."]</t>
    <t s="18">"Do not read 'morashah' but 'me'orasah' (betrothed), that the Torah is a bride betrothed to a man, they are the souls of Israel, etc."</t>
    <t s="19">And behold, all these four aspects are matters and subjects different from each other, for the matter of inheritance is something that comes by necessity, for a condition that contradicts what is written in the Torah is void110</t>
    <t s="20">for the commandment of inheritance is by necessity, etc.</t>
    <t s="21">And the matter of a gift is according to the will of the giver, for if the giver wishes to give the gift, it is good, and if not, it is not at all the possession of the recipient,</t>
    <t s="22">and the matter of "prepare yourself" is specifically through effort, that when one works well,</t>
    <t s="23">then the quality of his work which he worked in will come to him, and when the work is not so, he does not have it,</t>
    <t s="24">and this is the meaning of what they urge, saying "prepare yourself to study, because it is not an inheritance that comes by necessity,"</t>
    <t s="25">and it is also not a gift that is given even if one did not work so much,</t>
    <t s="26">but rather "prepare yourself" to toil yourself in the study of Torah, for through this you will succeed, etc.</t>
    <t s="27">And the matter of what the Torah is called a bride, this is also a different matter, etc.</t>
    <t s="28">And the explanation is111</t>
    <t s="29">that the fulfillment of Torah is impossible except through immense toil, etc., and as our Sages said112</t>
    <t s="30">"If you toiled and found, believe; if you did not toil and found, do not believe,"</t>
    <t s="31">for without toil it is impossible to find words of Torah,</t>
    <t s="32">and like the matter of their saying "prepare yourself to study Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you," lest you say it will come even without any toil at all, etc. And according to the effort that one works in the study of Torah, according to this will grow his understanding of Torah and the drawing down of Divinity that is drawn through his study and toil in Torah, etc. And about this our Sages said113</t>
    <t s="33">"Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him," that he draws down a drawing of Divinity in Torah,</t>
    <t s="34">and in this aspect of drawing down, the souls of Israel are called a groom and the Torah is called a bride, etc. And that the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews, this is specifically "opposite him,"</t>
    <t s="35">meaning, through the fact that the person reads and reviews.</t>
    <t s="36">And the matter of inheritance and gift is114</t>
    <t s="37">that all the matter of the performance of the commandments</t>
    <t s="38">[for study is great because it leads to action115]</t>
    <t s="39">which are clothed in physical things, is in order to refine the sparks of Tohu that fell into the broken vessels</t>
    <t s="40">[which are great lights,</t>
    <t s="41">in quantity and quality],</t>
    <t s="42">and through this aspect of refinement, through this they inherit the Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="43">and because this is not according to the measure of the refinement, etc.</t>
    <t s="44">[and as is known, the refinement at present is only in the seven lower Sefiros of Tohu, and through this they inherit automatically also the Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu,</t>
    <t s="45">as explained in the continuation of the discourse "Al Tetzar es Moav" by the Mitteler Rebbe116]</t>
    <t s="46">therefore it is called inheritance.</t>
    <t s="47">And when one merits to come to this inheritance, then they give him as a gift, meaning that there is drawn from Ein Sof a level above Tohu, which is the aspect of a gift, meaning that which is absolutely impossible to attain except by way of a gift alone.</t>
    <t s="48">And this means that this is above inheritance, for although even inheritance is not what one earns through his toil, nevertheless he has a connection to it, for why does a son inherit from his father? Because he comes from him, etc.</t>
    <t s="49">Thus, the matter of inheritance comes to one who has a connection, bond, and relationship with him, etc.</t>
    <t s="50">And similarly, it will be understood in the analogue, that according to how one refines the sparks of Tohu</t>
    <t s="51">[he becomes a "brother for good" to Esav]</t>
    <t s="52">therefore they give him, by way of inheritance, the aspect of the lights of Chochmah, Binah, and Daas of Tohu, etc.</t>
    <t s="53">And indeed, the matter of the gift is that which does not come through his action at all, etc.</t>
    <t s="54">And in the analogue, it is... that which no arousal from below reaches there, so the drawing down from there is a gift.</t>
    <t s="55">And this is what our Sages said117</t>
    <t s="56">"In the first three hours, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah,"</t>
    <t s="57">and seemingly, it is necessary to understand, did not our Sages say "Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him"?</t>
    <t s="58">And therefore, there should not be found in the world a single hour that is free, in which no one studies at that time at all,</t>
    <t s="59">for there is one who has no leisure during the day and studies at night,</t>
    <t s="60">and the main study is during the day, as the statement118</t>
    <t s="61">"We are workers of the day,"</t>
    <t s="62">and nevertheless they also said118</t>
    <t s="63">"Night was not created except for study,"</t>
    <t s="64">and thus it is found that all day and all night there is not a single free hour in which there is not found one of Israel who is not studying at that time,</t>
    <t s="65">and if so, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,</t>
    <t s="66">so what is the meaning of what it says that in the first three hours the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah, etc.</t>
    <t s="67">Also, the expression "sits and engages in Torah," what is it, etc.</t>
    <t s="68">But the explanation is as above, that what is said "Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,"</t>
    <t s="69">means that it is drawn according to his toil and effort,</t>
    <t s="70">and this is the precise meaning of the term "opposite him,"</t>
    <t s="71">and this is an aspect within the realm of measurement and limitation.</t>
    <t s="72">However, what is said "the first three hours" refers to the drawing down</t>
    <t s="73">[which is completely above the realm of measurement and limitation]</t>
    <t s="74">that is drawn in the aspect of a gift from above, even not through an arousal from below, etc. And therefore, about this it says "sits,"</t>
    <t s="75">similar to the lowering of one who sits</t>
    <t s="76">[for when he sits, his head is lowered downward],</t>
    <t s="77">and "engages in Torah."</t>
    <t s="78">And "first three" refers to the level above the realm of measurement and limitation, similar to the first three Sefiros that are brought in the books of Kabbalah in many places.</t>
    <t s="79">And nevertheless, even this level, which is completely above any arousal from below, is drawn through the fact that first there is the toil and inheritance mentioned above</t>
    <t s="80">[and this is the matter of "his study is in his hand"119],</t>
    <t s="81">for through this they give him as a gift also this level.</t>
    <t s="82">And in general,</t>
    <t s="83">behold, this is the general distinction between the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner aspect of Torah.</t>
    <t s="84">For the revealed aspect of Torah is the aspect of Torah that comes in measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="85">and as it is stated in the Gemara Menachos120</t>
    <t s="86">that it is possible for there to be a situation where a person learns the entire Torah,</t>
    <t s="87">thus there is a level in Torah that comes with limitation.</t>
    <t s="88">And nevertheless, it is said121</t>
    <t s="89">"It is longer than the measure of the earth and broader than the sea,"</t>
    <t s="90">and even more,</t>
    <t s="91">"And I was with Him... delights... before Him"122</t>
    <t s="92">which refers to the aspect of the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
    <t s="93">And this is the matter of the aspect of Panim and Achor of Torah,</t>
    <t s="94">meaning the aspect of the inner and revealed aspects of Torah,</t>
    <t s="95">and the aspect of Panim of Torah illuminates also in the aspect of Achor.</t>
    <t s="96">And from these two aspects of Panim and Achor that are in Torah, there is drawn afterward below, in the souls, the two aspects of Panim and Achor, and also that the aspect of Panim of souls illuminates in the aspect of Achor.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains Dovid's punishment for calling the Torah "songs" (Zemiros), because there is a higher level of Torah—the aspect of "delights before Him" (Sha'ashu'im)—which is the inner dimension, and his punishment of forgetfulness regarding carrying the Ark on the shoulder was measure for measure, as the Ark's tablets unified the aspects of Panim and Achor.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is also the explanation of what is said123</t>
    <t s="2">"Your statutes were songs to me in the house of my sojourning,"</t>
    <t s="3">and our Sages said124</t>
    <t s="4">that Dovid was punished for this.</t>
    <t s="5">And as explained in Likkutei Torah125</t>
    <t s="6">and in Torah Or126</t>
    <t s="7">and in many places127</t>
    <t s="8">the reason,</t>
    <t s="9">that what he was punished for calling the Torah "songs" is because although the Torah is in the aspect of songs,</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless, there is an aspect of Torah that is above this,</t>
    <t s="11">"song" (Shir),</t>
    <t s="12">and until there is an aspect even higher,</t>
    <t s="13">which is the aspect of "delights before Him,"</t>
    <t s="14">the aspect of the song of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is hidden from the eyes of all living128</t>
    <t s="15">which is the aspect of the inner dimension of Torah.</t>
    <t s="16">And this level that is in Torah,</t>
    <t s="17">which is in the aspect of "delights before Him,"</t>
    <t s="18">is above all measurement and limitation,</t>
    <t s="19">an aspect even higher than the aspect of songs of Torah,</t>
    <t s="20">but nevertheless, it is drawn down also below,</t>
    <t s="21">and therefore it was said to Dovid, "You called them songs"</t>
    <t s="22">(for he praised the Torah for being songs)</t>
    <t s="23">in astonishment,</t>
    <t s="24">since in the Torah there is a level that is an aspect even higher than the aspect of songs,</t>
    <t s="25">the aspect of "delights before Him,"</t>
    <t s="26">the aspect of song and the cantillation notes of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="27">And with this it will be understood why he was punished specifically with forgetfulness,</t>
    <t s="28">and the forgetfulness was regarding the matter of carrying the Ark on the shoulder,</t>
    <t s="29">for this punishment was measure for measure129.</t>
    <t s="30">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="31">that the matter of the Ark is that in it were the Tablets, as it is said130</t>
    <t s="32">"In the Ark there were only the two Tablets."</t>
    <t s="33">And the matter of the Tablets was that there was no division of Panim and Achor in them,</t>
    <t s="34">as it is stated in the Yerushalmi131</t>
    <t s="35">on the verse132</t>
    <t s="36">"written on both their sides, from this side and from that side,"</t>
    <t s="37">that from every side they could read them,</t>
    <t s="38">from their four sides, etc.,</t>
    <t s="39">meaning that</t>
    <t s="40">(it was entirely Panim and)</t>
    <t s="41">there was no division of Panim and Achor in it.</t>
    <t s="42">And this is also the matter of the commandment of carrying the Ark on the shoulder,</t>
    <t s="43">whose purpose is to connect the shoulder,</t>
    <t s="44">which is the aspect of Achor,</t>
    <t s="45">to the Ark,</t>
    <t s="46">in order to nullify it through this to the Ark</t>
    <t s="47">(in which were the Tablets),</t>
    <t s="48">similar to how it is in the Tablets that are in the Ark itself,</t>
    <t s="49">for although a scroll is written on both sides, Panim and Achor133</t>
    <t s="50">nevertheless, through the Tablets that are in the Ark, the aspects of Panim and Achor</t>
    <t s="51">(that are in the scroll)</t>
    <t s="52">become unified until they become one</t>
    <t s="53">(the aspect of Panim),</t>
    <t s="54">and similarly is the matter of the connection of the shoulder to the Ark</t>
    <t s="55">(in which are the Tablets).</t>
    <t s="56">And from this unification of the aspect of Panim and Achor that is through the Tablets,</t>
    <t s="57">one must draw down likewise in the study of Torah,</t>
    <t s="58">that the aspect of Achor of Torah</t>
    <t s="59">(the revealed aspect of Torah)</t>
    <t s="60">becomes unified with the aspect of Panim within it</t>
    <t s="61">(the inner dimension of Torah).</t>
    <t s="62">And this is why Dovid was punished specifically with forgetfulness,</t>
    <t s="63">for there is no forgetfulness before the Throne of Your glory,</t>
    <t s="64">from the perspective of the aspect of the inner dimension, forgetfulness does not apply.</t>
    <t s="65">For when a person is immersed</t>
    <t s="66">(liget)</t>
    <t s="67">in the inner dimension of his soul in some matter, then it is not possible that he will forget about it,</t>
    <t s="68">but rather specifically when his devotion to the matter is in the aspect of Achor,</t>
    <t s="69">in the aspect of the "back" of his attention.</t>
    <t s="70">And therefore he was punished with forgetfulness,</t>
    <t s="71">measure for measure.</t>
    <t s="72">Because in the Torah he praised the aspect of Achor,</t>
    <t s="73">the aspect of its songs alone.</t>
    <t s="74">And therefore the punishment of forgetfulness was in the commandment of carrying the Ark on the shoulder,</t>
    <t s="75">because its purpose is that through</t>
    <t s="76">(the Tablets that are in)</t>
    <t s="77">the Torah, the aspects of Panim and Achor</t>
    <t s="78">(that are in the Torah)</t>
    <t s="79">become unified in a manner that they are entirely Panim,</t>
    <t s="80">as above, "written... from this side and from that side," etc.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section teaches that Torah study must be preceded by "Barchu baTorah techilah" (blessing/initiating in Torah first), which is the service of prayer before study, and just as the aspect of Panim illuminates Achor in Torah, so too must this be reflected in the service of self-nullification and self-transformation before study.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">11)</t>
    <t s="1">a)</t>
    <t s="2">And behold, the study of Torah must be preceded by</t>
    <t s="3">(in the language of the Gemara134)</t>
    <t s="4">"Barchu baTorah techilah" (bless in the Torah first),</t>
    <t s="5">meaning the service of man before the Torah.</t>
    <t s="6">This is what Abba Binyamin would pray that his prayer be adjacent to his bed135,</t>
    <t s="7">for the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="8">as explained by the Alter Rebbe136,</t>
    <t s="9">in order that his study of Torah be after prayer,</t>
    <t s="10">for the prayer that precedes the study of Torah is similar to the matter of "Barchu baTorah techilah,"</t>
    <t s="11">"Barchu"</t>
    <t s="12">(from the term "drawing down")</t>
    <t s="13">in the Torah, etc.</t>
    <t s="14">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="15">that just as in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">the aspect of Panim illuminates also in the aspect of Achor</t>
    <t s="17">(as explained above at length),</t>
    <t s="18">so too must it be in the service</t>
    <t s="19">(of prayer)</t>
    <t s="20">that precedes it,</t>
    <t s="21">in the service of self-nullification and self-transformation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
